stem: Why may a medication that is substantially eliminated by the kidneys require dosage adjustment in a client with impaired renal function?

options.A: Renal impairment can reduce renal drug excretion and alter pharmacokinetics, so drug-specific renal dosing may be needed.
options.B: Renal impairment always increases renal drug clearance.
options.C: Kidney function has no effect on elimination of renally cleared medications.
options.D: All medications must be doubled when kidney function decreases.

rationale: FDA guidance notes that the kidneys eliminate many drugs and that impaired renal function typically decreases renal excretion, producing pharmacokinetic differences that can require a different dosage regimen for renally eliminated drugs.
educational_objective: Explain why renal impairment can require drug-specific dose modification.
source_document_title: Pharmacokinetics in Patients with Impaired Renal Function — Study Design, Data Analysis, and Impact on Dosing
source_locator: Background: kidneys eliminate many drugs; impaired renal function typically decreases renal excretion; renally eliminated drugs may require different dosage
source_claim_supported: Impaired renal function can decrease renal drug excretion and alter exposure, requiring drug-specific dosing changes.
